open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict creation on resubmission
open_points.text: “recorded once and then reused, never computed again” contradicts “Computed by the kernel when an implementation is submitted” and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time”
open_points.question: When an existing implementation is submitted again against the same corpus digest, must the kernel reuse the recorded verdict and its original TrialExecutions, or rerun every case and compute new admission evidence?
options: Reuse the existing AdmissionVerdict without executing trials
Run every case again and compute new TrialExecutions and a verdict
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the recorded verdict because the changed Meaning expressly says it is never computed again.

witness.initial: Implementation I already has a refused AdmissionVerdict for corpus digest C.
events: An authoring agent submits code equal to I again while the corpus still has digest C.
outcomes: The kernel returns the recorded refused verdict and performs no trial executions.
The kernel runs every case again and records fresh TrialExecutions from which it computes admission.
witness.observer: The submitting agent inspecting admission and trial evidence

open_points.subject: Determinism of admission for functions using undetected time or randomness
open_points.text: K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” while changed K-02 says code obtaining time or chance by another route “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other,” and changed M08 makes the first recorded result permanent.
open_points.question: Is an AdmissionVerdict a deterministic fact of the implementation and corpus, or may it permanently be whichever verdict resulted from the first admission execution of code whose undetected time or randomness changes its outputs?
options: The first observed trial outcomes determine and permanently fix the verdict for the pair
Admission must reject or otherwise prevent such output-dependent variability so the pair has a deterministic verdict
open_points.default_guess: Record and reuse the first verdict, because K-02 expressly says the alternate access is not detected and M08 says the verdict is recorded only once.

witness.initial: A contract has a trial case expecting a fixed output; its implementation obtains chance through a route the standard-library guards do not detect and sometimes returns that output and sometimes another valid output.
events: An agent submits the implementation for admission.
The kernel executes the active trial case.
outcomes: If that execution happens to match, an admitted verdict is recorded forever for the implementation and corpus pair.
The implementation is refused because K-05 requires the pair's admission verdict to be deterministic rather than dependent on the sampled execution.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and later runs using the activated implementation
